topics.label: Learning from human preferences: foundations
topics.summary: The original preference-comparison RL work and its first application to fine-tuning language models, which set up the reward-model-plus-RL recipe everything later builds on.

claims.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
claims.rationale: Introduces training a reward model from pairwise human comparisons and optimising a policy against it; the conceptual origin of RLHF.

claims.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
claims.rationale: First transfer of the preference-RL recipe to pretrained language models, including the KL penalty to a reference policy that remains standard.

claims.title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
claims.rationale: Shows RLHF beating supervised fine-tuning on summarisation with careful human evaluation; the clearest early demonstration that preference training works at scale.

topics.label: RLHF for instruction-following assistants
topics.summary: The three-stage SFT, reward model, PPO pipeline that produced InstructGPT and the first helpful-and-harmless assistants.

claims.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
claims.rationale: The policy-gradient algorithm used in almost every RLHF pipeline; read enough to understand the clipped objective and why it is stable.

claims.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
claims.rationale: The InstructGPT paper: the canonical description of the SFT then RM then PPO pipeline, labeller setup, and the alignment-tax discussion.

claims.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
claims.rationale: Anthropic's RLHF study: helpfulness versus harmlessness tension, iterated online data collection, and reward-model scaling trends.

topics.label: Reward modelling and its failure modes
topics.summary: How reward models are trained and evaluated, and how optimising against an imperfect proxy breaks down.

claims.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
claims.rationale: Quantifies Goodhart effects: proxy reward keeps rising while gold reward peaks then falls, as a function of KL and RM size, for both RL and best-of-n.

claims.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
claims.rationale: The standard benchmark for reward models; useful for seeing what RMs actually get wrong across chat, safety and reasoning.

claims.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
claims.rationale: Systematic catalogue of problems with human feedback, reward models and policy optimisation; the best single map of the field's weak points.

topics.label: Direct preference optimisation and RL-free alternatives
topics.summary: Methods that fold the reward model into the policy objective and train on preference pairs directly, replacing PPO.

claims.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
claims.rationale: Derives a closed-form reparameterisation of the KL-regularised RLHF objective so preferences train the policy directly; now the default alternative to PPO.

claims.title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Preferences
claims.rationale: Introduces the ΨPO framework and IPO; explains when DPO overfits because of the Bradley-Terry assumption and how to regularise.

claims.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
claims.rationale: Drops the need for paired preferences, training from binary good/bad labels; a useful contrast showing how loose the data requirements can be.

claims.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
claims.rationale: Length-normalised, reference-free variant of DPO; representative of the wave of DPO refinements and their evaluation on AlpacaEval and Arena-Hard.

topics.label: Constitutional AI and AI feedback
topics.summary: Replacing or supplementing human labels with model-generated critiques and preferences guided by written principles.

claims.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
claims.rationale: Defines the two-stage recipe: supervised self-critique and revision against a constitution, then RL from AI-generated preference labels (RLAIF).

claims.title: RLAIF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
claims.rationale: Head-to-head comparison of AI versus human preference labels on summarisation and dialogue, showing RLAIF matches RLHF; also introduces direct-RLAIF.

claims.title: Specific versus General Principles for Constitutional AI
claims.rationale: Tests how much the wording of the constitution matters, including a single 'do what is best for humanity' principle; sharpens intuitions about what CAI actually learns.
